title: Picture book pop up
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Design a visual identity and coordinated visitor materials for a one-room exhibition of handmade picture books at a neighborhood arts center. The show is called Fold and Find. It has 18 books across three tables organized by paper folds, movable pieces, and illustrated stories. Visitors include families with children ages five to nine. Two books per table can be handled, and the remaining books are display copies. Budget supports black ink plus one accent color on ordinary paper. Develop a system that helps families explore independently and lets staff update individual book information. Begin with an empty directory and choose the artifacts, tools, and file layout.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Fold and Find

A print kit for a one-room exhibition of 18 handmade picture books. The accordion, pull-tab and open-book characters link each table to the entrance sign, activity sheet and object labels.

## Print kit

| File in Print | Use |
| --- | --- |
| 01 Entrance.pdf | One welcome sign at the door |
| 02 Table signs.pdf | One sign per table, in table number order |
| 03 Family finding sheets.pdf | Two identical take-home sheets per page. Cut across the middle. |
| 04 Book labels - fillable.pdf | Six labels per page, one page per table. Fill in the actual titles and techniques or write on the lines after printing. |

Use white US Letter paper, single-sided, at actual size. The first two numbered slots at each table are for the books visitors may handle. Place the four display copies with their corresponding “Look only” labels. The hand and eye symbols carry these instructions in grayscale as well.

## Updating the exhibition

[Setup and updates](Staff/Setup%20and%20updates.pdf) covers layout, form editing and replacement printing. Keep one saved, editable copy of the labels as the inventory master. When changing a title, check that the text is legible at print size.

## Identity files

The four SVG files in Identity can be scaled for new signs. Use the same table names, numbers and characters throughout. Keep the artwork on white paper. Use solid black for text and outlines and blue (#164AB7) for the accent. For two-ink duplication, assign all blue artwork to the same blue ink. The wordmark uses outlined lettering so it can be placed without installing fonts.

# Fold and Find

A print kit and editable book register for a one-room exhibition of 18 handmade picture books. The numbered table symbols guide families to paper folds, movable pieces and illustrated stories. Each book label tells visitors whether they can handle the book.

## Print and install

Start with the [setup and visual identity guide](staff/setup-and-identity.pdf). Print single-sided on ordinary white US Letter paper at Actual Size or 100%. The PDFs contain black and a single named Vermilion spot color. The numbers, table symbols and hand/eye handling symbols also work in grayscale.

| Material | Copies and placement |
| --- | --- |
| [Welcome poster](print/01-welcome.pdf) | One at the entrance, with Book Hunt cards and pencils nearby. |
| [Table signs](print/02-table-signs.pdf) | One set. Place each numbered sign where visitors can read it from the aisle. |
| [Book Hunt cards](print/03-book-hunt.pdf) | Two cards per sheet. Cut across the dashed center line. |
| [Starter book labels](print/04-book-labels.pdf) | One set makes 18 labels, six per table. Cut along the dashed grid. |

## Fit the labels to the books

Open [Book register](staff/book-register.html) in a modern browser. Keep the files in the `staff` folder together so it works offline. The starter labels use shelf IDs and looking prompts because the book inventory was unspecified. The first two slots on each table are provisionally marked **TRY IT**. Before opening, match the books to their IDs and verify the two handling books at each table.

Edit a shelf ID to add the real title and tailor its prompt. Download the complete PDF or one replacement label. When swapping a handling book, clear the old slot, mark the replacement and reprint both labels. Save a register backup after editing, then use **Open a backup** to continue on another browser or computer.

Label PDFs support Western European letters and common punctuation. The live preview flags text that exceeds the label space or uses unsupported characters. A saved backup also works when browser storage is disabled.
